summary: Summation No. 13 covers non-military Occupation activities in Japan for October 1946, with statistical data mostly for September. The Diet completed its 114-day session on 12 October after passing the new Constitution (298-2 in the Peers, 342-5 in the Representatives), approved by the Privy Council on 29 October for promulgation on 3 November and effect on 3 May 1947. The Land Reform Bill passed on 11 October and MacArthur praised it. The report also covers the National Congress of Industrial Unions' 'October offensive' strikes, the Labor Relations Adjustment Act, a 20 percent rice ration increase, Bank of Japan note circulation of 70.6 billion yen, war indemnity cancellation and the capital levy, holding company liquidation plans, the Tokyo war crimes trial (French, Soviet and general-preparation phases), cholera eradication, reopening of Japanese history courses and the teacher screening. It also gives production series for coal, metals, textiles, power and communications, with the full constitutional text. Historians will find it useful for the political and legal transition and economic recovery indicators.
highlights: On 6-7 October the Diet gave final approval to the new Constitution (House of Peers 298 to 2, House of Representatives 342 to 5); the Privy Council approved it on 29 October, promulgation was set for 3 November and effect for 3 May 1947.
The 90th Diet, 20 June to 12 October, was the longest in Japanese history; it passed 94 other bills, raised members' pay from 230 to 1,750 yen a month, and received 878 petitions from citizens.

The Diet passed the Land Reform Bill on 11 October: absentee landlords must sell all land, resident landlords may keep one cho (four in Hokkaido), and local commissions of five tenants, three landlords and two owner-cultivators run purchases; MacArthur called it a farmers' Bill of Rights.

The National Congress of Industrial Unions' 'October offensive' produced the widest strike activity since the surrender (coal, press and radio, electric power); Yoshida denounced political general strikes on 15 October, and radio stations were closed 5-25 October.

The Government raised the basic rice ration about 20 percent from 1 November and raised the official rice price; imported food releases fell to their lowest level since June and canned food distribution stopped on 31 October.
Bank of Japan notes reached 70,599,401,000 yen on 31 October; Supplemental Budgets 1 and 2 totalled 9,744,028,337 yen, and war indemnity cancellation and the capital levy laws moved ahead.

SCAP ordered 'Tokyo Rose' (Iva Toguri) released from Sugamo on 25 October; the Philippine trials sentenced eight of ten defendants to death, and the Tokyo tribunal heard the French, Soviet and general-preparation phases of the prosecution.

Coal output was 1,742,400 tons in September, cotton yarn rose by 6,407,000 pounds and cotton cloth doubled, while the Imperial Oil strike cut crude oil to 15,691 kiloliters; cholera was declared eradicated and 339,614 Japanese were repatriated.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 13 (October 1946), table of contents for Parts I-IV, and list of 89 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: passage of the new Constitution, party and labor politics, war crimes, economic indicators, rice ration increase, finance and social developments.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization under SCAP
sections.summary: Single paragraph stating there was no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during October.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Final Diet passage of the Constitution on 6-7 October, the Social Democrats' convention, party merger talks, strikes, war crimes figures and the tribunal's tenth phase.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Land Reform Bill passed 11 October, September industrial indexes, coal at 1,742,400 tons, strikes, rice ration up 20 percent, note circulation of 70.6 billion yen and 466 reparations plants.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Repatriation of 339,614 Japanese, penicillin licences, vaccination of 17,000,000 children, reopening of history courses, teacher screening totals, Fire Prevention Week and the radio strike settlement.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics including the Constitution's text, public safety and intelligence, and legal affairs and war crimes including the International Military Tribunal's French, Soviet and general-preparation phases.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Final Constitution vote of 298-2 and 342-5, full official text, the longest Diet session, Social Democratic convention, strikes, the Emperor's tour of Aichi and Gifu, the 877-name purge list.

sections.title: The Constitution: passage, amendments and Kanamori commentary
sections.summary: Diet completed action on 7 October; Peers added universal suffrage and civilian Cabinet clauses; Privy Council vote 29 October; Kanamori's commentary on popular sovereignty and the Emperor as symbol.

sections.title: Official translation of the Constitution of Japan
sections.summary: Certified text of the Constitution's preamble and Chapters I-X, including Article 9 renouncing war and Article 15 guaranteeing universal adult suffrage.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: The 90th Session ran 20 June to 12 October and passed 94 bills; 878 petitions received; Diet pay rose from 230 to 1,750 yen monthly; 22 bills passed 25 September to 12 October.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Right wing won the Social Democrats' 28-30 September convention under Tetsu Katayama; 33 Diet members formed the New People's Party; Liberal-Progressive and Progressive-Cooperative merger talks stalled.

sections.title: Labor and Politics
sections.summary: Party reaction to the NCIU 'October Labor Offensive' strikes; Yoshida's 15 October Osaka speech calling political general strikes an abuse of labor's right.

sections.title: The Emperor and Local Government
sections.summary: Emperor met MacArthur 17 October and toured Aichi and Gifu 21-26 October; a 72-member Local Government System Investigation Commission was appointed 11 October.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: Official alphabetical list of 877 top-ranking officials removed under the 4 January Purge Directive, published by major newspapers in October.

sections.title: Structural and Personnel Changes
sections.summary: War Inquiry Commission abolished 30 September; Administrative System Investigation Board under Yoshida created; Saburo Ota named chief of the Yokosuka Liaison Office.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety and Intelligence
sections.summary: NCIU strikes and daily five-minute blackouts, 41 Formosans on trial, 152,437 crimes in August, new police college, juvenile crime section, 62,661 prisoners and fire losses of 108,430,380 yen.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal and War Crimes
sections.summary: Lese-majeste charges dropped 9 October; 19 constitutional implementing bills drafted; 1,595 occupation court cases; Tokyo Rose released; Philippine trials sentenced eight to death; tribunal phases on French and Soviet relations.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and Japanese Judicial Administration
sections.summary: Trial of 41 Formosans before a mixed commission; dismissal of lese-majeste charges praised by MacArthur; Provisional Legislative Investigating Committee ended 110 days' work with 19 draft bills.

sections.title: Military Occupation Courts; Apprehension and Investigation of War Criminals
sections.summary: 1,543 guilty verdicts among 1,595 cases; 817 internees in Sugamo; 754 prisoners held in the Philippines; atrocity case table; release of Iva Toguri; Australian and British investigations.

sections.title: Prosecution of War Criminals (Philippines trials)
sections.summary: 247 cases in preparation in Japan; five Philippine trials of ten defendants ended with eight death sentences, plus five and 25 years; Negros civilian killings cases of Yamamoto, Nishikawa and others.

sections.title: International Prosecution: Eighth Phase (French Relations)
sections.summary: Tribunal evidence on Japan's September 1940 entry into French Indo-China under ultimatum, the 1941 Vichy protocol and the 9 March 1945 takeover.

sections.title: International Prosecution: Ninth Phase (Soviet Relations)
sections.summary: From 8 October the prosecution traced Japanese plans from the 1920 Siberian expedition to the Kwantung Army's 1,100,000 men; witnesses Tatsugi, Kasahara, Kawabe, Tereshkin, Sejima and Matsumura.

sections.title: International Prosecution: Tenth Phase (General Preparations)
sections.summary: Opened 21 October on industrial preparation for war and enforced cartelization; testimony of Liebert and documents on total control of industry.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Detailed September production and October policy data for agriculture, mining, industry, textiles, utilities, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property control.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Land Reform Bill terms and MacArthur's 12 October statement, 9,002,000-ton rice estimate, fertilizer plans, and September fish landings of 86,075 tons.

sections.title: Rural Land Reform
sections.summary: Absentee landlords must sell; resident landlords keep one cho; commissions of tenants, landlords and owner-cultivators run purchases within two years; MacArthur's praise on 12 October.

sections.title: Crop Production, Fertilizer and Mulberry Acreage
sections.summary: Rice at 9,002,000 metric tons, record sweet potatoes, falling wheat and barley estimates, phosphatic and potassic fertilizer distribution and preliminary mulberry acreage.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: September landings up 6,707 tons to 86,075; coastal whaling took 431 whales in seven weeks; 40,518 kiloliters of fuel oil arranged for Antarctic whaling; Matsukawa-ura harbor repairs.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Log output of 485,360,000 board feet, charcoal at 57 percent of plan, coal at 1,742,400 tons, lignite goals, and Imperial Oil's strike cutting crude to 15,691 kiloliters.

sections.title: Forestry: Logs, Lumber, Plywood and Charcoal
sections.summary: Highest log production since March; plywood fell to 14,068,000 square feet; first 200 tons of imported soybean-casein glue arrived; charcoal incentives for workers.

sections.title: Coal and Lignite
sections.summary: Coal 1,742,400 tons (Kyushu 941,500); 1947-48 plan of 355,000 miners; stockpiles of 959,000 tons; lignite 231,755 tons; Coal Board 75,000,000 yen exploration program.

sections.title: Petroleum and Mining Industry
sections.summary: Crude oil fell to 15,691 kiloliters after the 6 September Imperial Oil strike; copper near 1,500 tons, lead 416 tons, zinc 1,910 tons, gold 125 kilograms monthly.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke 113,000 tons, aluminum 836 tons, copper, zinc, rubber supply to run out by 1 January 1947, cement 95,431 tons, housing program, chemicals at 31 percent of minimum needs, machinery.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Wine output 21,466 hectoliters from 554 wineries, pulp and paper, glass, brick and tile, electrical goods, trucks, rubber goods, leather, agricultural equipment and consumer products.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton yarn up nearly 50 percent and cloth output doubled, 35 cotton cargoes totalling 649,871 bales shipped, raw silk 800 bales short of goal, rayon, wool, bast fibers and knit goods.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 105,806 motor vehicles, freight tonnage up, 2,271,341,000 kWh generated amid drought and rationing to industry, seven hydroelectric plants adding 30,030 kW, gas coal shortage.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Radio strike closing stations 5-25 October, telephones up four percent, restoration of postal savings records (35,000,000 of 200,000,000 rebuilt), mail volumes, equipment output and Ministry staffing.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Labor Relations Adjustment Act promulgated 12 October; 13,622 unions with 3,936,815 members; widest strikes since surrender; wage and cost-of-living gap narrowing; public works hiring and 123 arrests over indentured labor in Hokkaido.

sections.title: Labor Legislation and Organizations
sections.summary: Labor Standards, unemployment insurance, workmen's compensation and seamen's bills; union statistics, seamen's union dissension and the Kanto Employers' Association conference.

sections.title: Labor Relations, Education, Wages and Employment
sections.summary: Strike record of the NCIU offensive, labor education conferences, wage incentive policy for coal, eight-hour day policy, employment exchange expansion by 4,120 workers, and textile worker rice rations.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Washington approved revised export and import programs for 1 July-31 December 1946; first postwar tengujo paper shipment to the US, 9,187 tons of German potash received, salt diverted to Korea.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Staple ration raised from 1 November with higher rice price, imported food releases lowest since June, fertilizer and soda prices, rents rising, textiles and consumer goods, hoarded silk recovered.

sections.title: Food, Fertilizer and Chemicals
sections.summary: Rice ration increase, ending of imported canned food distribution 31 October, vegetable and fish prices, ammonium sulfate shipments, phosphatic and potassic fertilizer and soda prices.

sections.title: Coal, Rents, Textiles and Consumer Goods
sections.summary: Rents rising, textile distribution, rubber footwear, matches, soap, 2,200 tons of imported salt and cigarette monopoly sales of 240,000,000 'Peaces' monthly.

sections.title: Violations and Controls
sections.summary: September violations below the 1946 monthly average; special drive recovered hoarded foodstuffs, textiles and previously unreported silk turned in to the Japanese Government.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes of 70,599,401,000 yen, Bank of Tokyo authorized 11 October, 7 percent United Funds Bank dividend, national debt of 223 billion yen and supplementary budgets of 9.7 billion.

sections.title: Money and Banking
sections.summary: Foreign exchange for Okinawan repatriates, currency circulation, Bank of Japan statement, holdings of 47,890,000,000 yen in government bonds, and the Deposit Bureau losses bill.

sections.title: Public Finance
sections.summary: Taxation and revenue, national debt rise to 223,052,000,000 yen, Supplemental Budgets 1 and 2 with pay raises for government employees, local government finance and Imperial Household.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Allied property and bank deposits in Japan, dissolved organizations, patents, looted property and precious metals in SCAP custody, five holding companies' liquidation plans, 466 reparations plants.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare (repatriation, cholera eradication, medical supplies) plus education, religion, arts and media, including the reopening of history courses and magazines.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Welfare payments of 127,507,087 yen to 2,852,911 people, repatriation of 339,614, penicillin licences, cholera eradicated, 17,000,000 children vaccinated against diphtheria, nutrition survey and vital statistics.

sections.title: Public Welfare and Repatriation
sections.summary: Welfare aid and relief organization; 339,614 Japanese repatriated 30 September-27 October and 38,117 foreign nationals left, mostly Ryukyuans; hospital patients chart.

sections.title: Veterinary, Dental, Nursing and Medical Supply
sections.summary: Dairy score card inspection, 938 dentists re-established, medical supply production chart, penicillin factory approval and narcotics control arrests.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine, Nutrition and Vital Statistics
sections.summary: Last cholera cases week ending 5 October, diphtheria immunization, communicable disease charts, venereal disease survey, Tokyo calorie intake up 35 percent, marriages up 39 percent.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Imperial Rescript reading ended 8 October, Japanese history courses reopened by 15 October memorandum, 215,846 teachers screened, church and cultural property items, radio, press and magazine comment.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Rescript ceremonies abrogated, new history texts, Education Reform Committee subcommittees, inspector training, teacher screening (1,126 removed, 107 dismissed, 56 reinstated), coeducation, graduation statistics.

sections.title: Religion, Arts and Monuments
sections.summary: Church of Christ in Japan adopted a constitution and creed; $25,000 pastor relief fund distributed; eight field examiners hired and 1,261,000 yen allotted for cultural properties.

sections.title: Media of Expression
sections.summary: Fire Prevention and Daily Life Security Law campaigns, women's organizations, 'Liberal Thinkers' radio series, press and magazine comment, 1,250 new magazines, films, theater pageant and libraries.
